multiplechoiceresponse.p: You must change a handful of rows in a large table. The safest procedure is:

choice.div: Run the WHERE clause as a SELECT first, then UPDATE inside a transaction.
Run the UPDATE without a WHERE and re-insert the wrong rows.
Export the whole table, edit it in a spreadsheet, and re-import it.

div.p: Preview the affected rows, then act in a transaction so the change is atomic and can be rolled back. An UPDATE without a WHERE has no undo.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A LEFT JOIN suddenly behaves like an INNER JOIN. The usual cause is:

choice.div: A condition on the right table placed in WHERE instead of ON.
COUNT was used instead of SUM.

div.p: Filtering the right table in WHERE discards the NULL-extended rows, so the unmatched left rows disappear. Move the condition into the ON clause to keep them.

choiceresponse.p: Which statements about keys and constraints are true? Select all that apply.

choice.div: A foreign key references another table's primary key.
NOT NULL and UNIQUE are rules the database enforces.
Constraints are only advisory and can be ignored by writers.
Indexing the columns you filter and join on speeds up lookups.

div.p: Constraints are enforced by the engine, not by convention — that is their value. Indexes help reads at a cost in write time and space.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: AVG(score) can differ from what you expect when the column contains NULLs because:

choice.div: NULLs are ignored, so the denominator is the count of non-null values.
AVG rounds to the nearest integer.

div.p: Aggregates skip NULLs. If "no score" should count as zero, coalesce it explicitly — do not assume the engine agrees with you.
